quandoUsar: One or more measures over time, when the shape of the trend matters more than an isolated value.
Comparing the current period with the previous one or with a target, using a dashed series (`dashed`).
Dashboards with a range switch (7, 14, 30 days): with the same `key`s, the lines transform instead of redrawing.
quandoEvitar: Use `sparkline` for a compact trend next to a number, with no axes or legend.
Use `bar-chart` to compare a measure period by period, reading each bar against the average.
Use `brush-chart` for dense series where the user needs to zoom into a time window.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, move the crosshair to the previous or next point; `↓` and `↑` do the same.
`Page Up` moves forward and `Page Down` moves back about a sixth of the points.
Go to the first and last point.
Releases the crosshair and hides the tooltip.
On the legend buttons, hide or show the series.
Moves through the legend buttons and the chart; on receiving focus by keyboard, the crosshair starts at the most recent point.

acessibilidade: The chart area is a `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` reads the current point with the value of each visible series; SVG, axes, and tooltip are `aria-hidden`.
There is a hidden summary with the range and the last value of each series, and a hidden table with all points, whose first column uses `categoryLabel`.
The legend buttons use `aria-pressed`, and a hidden series gets a struck-through name, not just a missing color; `label` is required, and `loading` marks the figure with `aria-busy`.
movimento: The first time it enters the viewport with data, the lines draw from left to right in about 0.8 s.
Swapping `data` transforms each line from its current shape, even with a different number of points, while the scale and gridlines readjust; hiding a series flattens it to the baseline.
The crosshair slides between points and the tooltip follows it on its own spring, switching sides before leaving the chart; with “reduced motion”, all of this is immediate.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is fixed by the `height` prop (220 px by default); the value axis takes 48 px on the right.
The date axis shows at most one label every 76 px, counting from the most recent; on touch, pressing and dragging horizontally moves the crosshair.
desempenho: A single painter writes the paths straight to the SVG on each frame, without re-rendering React; the hidden screen-reader table has one row per point, which is heavy with thousands of points.
notasIA: `label`, `data`, and `series` are required; each point carries `values` indexed by the series `key`, and a missing value counts as zero, not as a gap.
Only points with `axisLabel` get an axis label; the first series uses the accent color with a filled area, and the rest stay in neutral tones until they receive `color`.
Use `onActiveChange` to feed a highlight number outside the chart and `loading` to keep the current lines faded while the next range loads.
